evidence.title: Fed’s Warsh Rebuked by Investors Craving a Real Inflation Fight
evidence.body: [e001:f01] Bond traders and Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh are in agreement on a crucial point: The central bank’s fight against inflation still seems far from over.

evidence.title: US bond investors avoid big bets ahead of Fed meeting
evidence.body: [e002:f01] Uncertainty over inflation has prompted them to favour high-quality assets while waiting for clearer signals on the direction of US interest rates. [e002:f02] According to Reuters , most market participants expect the Fed to keep its benchmark interest rate at 3.50%-3.75% at the end of its two-day policy meeting, which concludes on Wednesday (29 July). [e002:f03] However, a surge in energy prices earlier this month and renewed concerns over inflation have made the outlook for monetary policy more difficult to predict. [e002:f04] US consumer inflation slowed to 3.5% in June 2026. [e002:f05] However, the figure remains well above the Fed’s 2% target. [e002:f06] Amid the uncertainty, portfolio managers see little reason to aggressively extend bond duration or increase exposure to riskier assets. [e002:f07] Both indicators are expected to provide clearer signals on the Fed’s next policy moves. [e002:f08] According to Granet, smaller positions and disciplined risk management are more appropriate strategies ahead of the Fed’s decision on Wednesday (29 July). [e002:f09] However, he believes taking large bets ahead of this week’s Fed meeting would not be a prudent move. [e002:f10] According to CME’s FedWatch tool on Monday (27 July), markets priced in a 36% probability of an interest rate hike this week, up from 16% a week earlier. [e002:f11] "The more important question is whether the threshold for the next policy move becomes higher or lower." Oil Shock However, not all investors believe the Fed will follow market expectations and raise rates again. [e002:f12] This suggests investors still expect economic growth to remain strong, supported by optimism over AI developments and capital investment. [e002:f13] According to him, the combination of no near-term rate hikes, stronger economic growth expectations and rising real yields is making it more difficult for investors to determine bond duration strategies and positions along the yield curve ahead of the Fed meeting. [e002:f14] He said these instruments still allow investors to build high-quality portfolios with yields of around 5.5%-6%. [e002:f15] Therefore, short- to medium-term US government bonds look more attractive to us," he said. ページ: 1 2 すべて表示 Add as a preferred source on Google 1%+持株モニター 上場企業の1%以上の持株比率を持つ株主を簡単にモニタリング。 [e002:f16] こちらをクリック 共有: 最新ニュース BNBRは最高の純対外売を記録 27 Jul 2026 20:30 Kimia Farmaのコミサリス役、Sumarjati Arjoso氏が死去 27 Jul 2026 18:10 DMASは2026年上期にIDR 1.15 trillionのマーケティング販売を記録 27 Jul 2026 17:30 ジャカルタ総合株価指数（JCI）は減、ルピア安、投資家はBIの総裁の過渡期に懸念 27 Jul 2026 16:45 シンガポール、人材流出防止のための税制優遇を検討 27 Jul 2026 12:40 # Hot Topic JCI stocks Indonesia Iran earnings report rupiah China index Sheets Sell 人気ニュース CXMTが中国のチップ産業復活の象徴に 26 Jul 2026 10:05 ホルムズ海峡のタンカー航行数が減少、石油供給リスクが高まる 26 Jul 2026 19:00 シンガポール、人材流出防止のための税制優遇を検討 27 Jul 2026 12:40 ブラックロック：投資家はポートフォリオに金を引き続き保有すべき 26 Jul 2026 14:00 ドイツのスタートアップRevolta、家庭用ナトリウムイオン電池を発表 27 Jul 2026 07:00。

evidence.title: S&P Global to acquire majority stake in Agusto & Co. in Africa expansion
evidence.body: [e003:f01] Samson Akintaro Senior Analyst 3 min read Follow Us on Google Discover S&P Global has agreed to acquire a majority stake in Agusto & Co., one of Africa’s leading credit rating agencies, in a deal aimed at strengthening its presence in the continent’s domestic credit ratings market. [e003:f02] The two organisations disclosed this on Tuesday in a joint statement made available to Nairametrics. [e003:f03] The transaction, which is subject to regulatory approvals, will see the global financial intelligence and ratings company partner with Agusto & Co., whose operations span Nigeria, Kenya, Rwanda and Ghana. [e003:f04] Although the financial terms of the deal were not disclosed, both companies said the partnership is expected to accelerate the growth of credit markets across Africa by combining S&P Global’s international expertise with Agusto & Co.’s regional knowledge. [e003:f05] Also Read CBN lowers T-bill yield as oversubscription jumps sevenfold Nigerian equities lose N648 billion as TIP, NREIT lead broad mid-week sell-off Nigeria’s rate hikes may be hurting growth more than prices, Fasua warns What they are saying According to the statement, the investment will complement the growth strategy of S&P Global Ratings in Africa by expanding market insights, improving credit transparency and supporting investors and issuers across the continent. [e003:f06] Yann Le Pallec, President of S&P Global Ratings, said the acquisition demonstrates the company’s long-term commitment to Africa’s capital markets. [e003:f07] “ We are delighted to partner with Agusto & Co. to strengthen our domestic ratings presence across Africa,” Le Pallec said. [e003:f08] He added that Africa presents significant growth opportunities, noting that combining S&P Global’s global expertise with Agusto & Co.’s local market knowledge would foster informed analysis, strengthen market dialogue and boost investor confidence both within Africa and internationally. [e003:f09] According to Adelekan, the partnership fulfils the vision of the company’s late founder to affiliate with a leading global credit rating agency. [e003:f10] He said Agusto & Co. has spent more than three decades building a trusted credit rating institution across Africa and believes the partnership will create new opportunities for market participants while supporting the development of transparent and resilient credit markets. [e003:f11] Despite the acquisition, Agusto & Co. will continue operating as a separate ratings entity, issuing its own credit ratings and methodologies in line with applicable regulatory requirements. [e003:f12] Regulatory approvals pending The transaction remains subject to customary closing conditions, including approvals from relevant regulators in the jurisdictions where Agusto & Co. operates. [e003:f13] S&P Global also stated that the acquisition is not expected to have a material impact on the financial performance of either S&P Global or S&P Global Ratings. [e003:f14] The acquisition marks one of the most significant investments by a global credit ratings provider in Africa’s domestic ratings industry. [e003:f15] In May, the global rating agency upgraded Nigeria’s long-term foreign and local currency credit ratings to ‘B’ from ‘B-’ , citing President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s economic reforms, improved foreign exchange liquidity, stronger fiscal revenues, and rising external reserves. [e003:f16] The global agency also affirmed Nigeria’s short-term sovereign ratings at ‘B’, while raising the country’s national scale ratings to ‘ngA+/ngA-1’ from ‘ngBBB+/ngA-2’, with a stable outlook.

[e005:f07] Advertisement “This transaction underscores our commitment to supporting growth and transparency in local credit markets throughout the continent. evidence.title: What a divided Fed means for investors
evidence.body: [e004:f01] The Fed opted to [hold interest rates steady](https:// at the second meeting led by Chairman [Kevin Warsh](https:// But between his commentary about inflation and the dissenting coalition of policymakers, investors are growing increasingly confident that the Fed's next move will be an increase. [e004:f02] While the hold was widely expected by markets, three policymakers broke with the committee's decision to instead call for higher rates at this week's meeting. [e004:f03] That marked the highest number of members pushing for an increase since September 2016, according to Ian Lygen, head of U.S. rates strategy at BMO Capital Markets. [e004:f04] Back in 2016, the Fed went on to keep rates unchanged at its next meeting in November with two dissenters. [e004:f05] But by December of that year, the committee unanimously voted on a 25-basis-point increase. [e004:f06] Fed funds futures trading now suggests a more than 57% likelihood of a quarter-point increase at the September meeting, according to CME's [FedWatch](https:// tool. [e004:f07] About 53% of [Kalshi traders](https:// predict that the Fed will hike rates, compared with 43% betting on another hold. [e004:f08] "September remains a live meeting." Stephen Douglass, chief economist at NISA Investment Advisors, said the three members' dissentions could signal the Fed landed on a "hawkish hold." Still, Douglass said he still expected the Fed's next move to be a cut in March of next year. [e004:f09] Warsh said the Fed was focused on [getting inflation down](https:// to its preferred annual rate of 2% after years of hotter readings. [e004:f10] The problem: Getting there likely means policy tightening, according to DoubleLine Capital CEO [Jeffrey Gundlach](https:// "If you really want to get to 2%, I think you have to raise interest rates," Gundlach [said Wednesday](https:// on CNBC's "Closing Bell." ## [](http:// response In the meantime, unease about a future with potentially tighter monetary policy helped put investors in a risk-off mood on Wednesday. [e004:f11] The [S&P 500](https:// tumbled 1.5% in Wednesday's session, marking the worst second "Fed day" for a new chief in recent history, according to Bespoke Investment Group. [e004:f12] The blue-chip [Dow Jones Industrial Average](https:// dropped more than 2% on Wednesday, its [largest daily decline](https:// since President Donald Trump's tariff policy hampered markets in April 2025. [e004:f13] [Image 1: hide content](https:// S&P 500, 1 -day "Financial markets are still wrestling with the shift in Fed leadership," said Josh Jamner, senior investment strategy analyst at ClearBridge Investments. [e004:f14] He described increased price volatility under a Warsh-led Fed as "more of a feature than a bug." The [30-year Treasury](https:// yield climbed more than 10 basis points on Wednesday to reach its highest level [since July 2007](https:// The benchmark [10-year Treasury](https:// yield rose above the key 4.6% level, while shorter-dated yields pulled back as the meeting showed that the Fed appeared willing to wait to respond to inflation. ! [e004:f15] 30-year Treasury Fixed income investors like Gundlach said that these moves are showing the Fed that they must return to hiking to achieve their goals on inflation. [e004:f16] "The long bond yield went up significantly after the press conference," Gundlach said.

evidence.title: 米国：7月CB消費者信頼感は現況悪化で低下
evidence.body: [e006:f01] これは、市場予想中央値（92.4）や筆者予想（92.0）を下回る結果である。 [e006:f02] 地政学リスクやエネルギーコスト負担が逆風となり、指数は引き続き低位で推移。 [e006:f03] 期待指数は74.7（前月74.7：改定前74.4）と横ばいを維持し先行きの底割れは回避された。 [e006:f04] 一方、現状指数は114.9（前月118.5：改定前116.4）と前月比3.6ポイント低下した。 [e006:f05] 2. 悲観バイアスは継続も、地政学リスクへの過度な警戒は後退 発表元によると、「7月も経済に対する悲観的なバイアスが継続」している。 [e006:f06] 回答者の「価格」「石油・ガス」への言及頻度は減少したものの高水準しており、さらに「食料品価格」に関する言及は増加した。 [e006:f07] 一方、「戦争」「地政学」「紛争」への言及は減少しており、中東情勢がインフレに与える影響への過度な懸念は和らぎつつある。 [e006:f08] ただし、7月に発生した一時的な戦闘激化が速報値に十分反映されていない可能性もあり、改定値で再び言及が増加する余地を残している。 [e006:f09] また、雇用や失業に関する言及が微増しており、労働市場の実態はFOMCの想定ほど強固ではない可能性を示唆している。 [e006:f10] 3. 景気・雇用懸念が根強く、所得期待も縮小 項目別にみると、先行き不透明感の和らぎが現状判断の悪化を一部相殺しているものの、足元の景気・雇用環境に対する見方はともに弱まった。 [e006:f11] 現状指数の構成項目では、現在の景気判断（「良い」-「悪い」）が＋1.1（前月＋3.7：改定前＋3.5）へ低下したほか、現在の雇用機会判断（「充分」-「困難」）も＋3.1（前月＋3.8：改定前＋2.4）へとプラス幅を縮小させ、足元の雇用に対する見方は後退した。 [e006:f12] 6カ月後の雇用に対する見方（「多くなる」-「少なくなる」）は▲8.6（前月▲9.9：改定前▲10.4）とマイナス幅を縮小させたものの、依然としてマイナス圏に沈んでおり雇用の先行きへの懸念は根強く残っている。 [e006:f13] 6カ月後の景気に対する見方（「良くなる」-「悪くなる」）は▲3.3（前月▲1.8：改定前▲1.3）へと悪化し、悲観論が若干強まった。 [e006:f14] さらに、6カ月後の収入に対する見方（「増加する」-「減少する」）は＋7.3（前月＋7.8：改定前＋7.6）と低下しており、ガソリン価格の再上昇などを背景に所得増加への期待は幾分弱まっている。 [e006:f15] 4. インフレ心理の定着（粘着化）リスクへの警戒 インフレ面では、1年先のインフレ見通しが5.5％（前月5.9％）へと低下したものの、依然として高水準での推移が続いている。
